questions.q: In the final version of main(), how many Slack alerts does a single run send?
options: Zero, since logging already covers it
Exactly one -- a success message or a failure message, never both and never neither
One for every function called during the run
Three, one for each major step
questions.explain: The try block sends a success alert after all three steps complete, and the except block sends a failure alert instead if anything raises -- exactly one alert per run, either way.

questions.q: Why does the wrap-up split the generic `except Exception` into separate `except RuntimeError` and `except requests.exceptions.RequestException` blocks?
options: Python requires at least two except blocks per try statement
A failed user-setup step and a failed API call need different responses, so distinguishing them tells whoever reads the alert where to look first
RuntimeError and RequestException cannot both be imported in the same file
It makes the script run in parallel instead of sequentially
questions.explain: Catching specific exceptions separately, the habit from the logging and error-handling lesson, lets the alert point at the right place to investigate -- the store's server versus the warehouse API -- instead of a single generic failure message.

questions.q: Why does the lesson still redirect launch_store.py's output to a log file with `>> ... 2>&1`, even though it isn't a recurring cron job?
options: Redirection is only useful for scheduled jobs, not one-off runs
A one-off run started by whoever is on duty still benefits from never letting output disappear, the same habit from the scheduling lesson
Python scripts cannot produce any stderr output
It makes the script execute faster
questions.explain: Even a manually triggered, on-demand script benefits from the same principle the scheduling lesson established: unredirected output has nowhere to go and effectively disappears, whether the job is scheduled or run by hand.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend a capstone README emphasize, beyond what the code itself already shows?
options: A line-by-line restatement of every function's code
The reasoning behind the design choices -- why idempotent setup, env-var secrets, and specific exception handling were used
The exact number of lines of code written
A list of every Python keyword used in the script
questions.explain: The lesson argues that explaining the reasoning behind design choices tells an employer more about judgment than the code alone, since the code shows what was built but not necessarily why.

questions.q: According to the lesson, which course comes next in this path after Python & Bash Automation?
options: Kubernetes Orchestration
Docker & Containers
Infrastructure as Code with Terraform
Linux Administration
questions.explain: The course closes by pointing to Docker & Containers as the next step in the path, building on reliable automation scripts by packaging what they manage into containers.
